title: Albert Grunow diatom collection at Vienna: sample numbers across raw material, slides, catalogue, drawings and annotated books

principal_upgrade.previous_state: A+ comparator; one sample number through every medium requested
principal_upgrade.new_state: S-level collection-system architecture. NHM Vienna now publicly documents the component types, scale, numbering systems and the catalogue's cross-referential functions in enough detail to establish that sample numbers were deliberate cross-media retrieval infrastructure.
principal_upgrade.guard: S applies to the documented architecture of Grunow's collection and catalogue. A specific sample-number chain from raw material through historical slide, drawing and annotated publication remains to be selected and closed item by item.

historical_curation_evidence.instructions: Grunow left eleven pages of instructions about the collection and catalogue. The 2023 NHM study publishes/analyses these instructions, including an English translation and palaeographic aid.
historical_curation_evidence.interpretive_value: The catalogue was an active curation and retrieval instrument, not merely a later museum inventory. It coordinated sample identity across materially different states and media.

digitisation_sequence.first: QR-code folders in drawing collection to assign unique stable identifiers
digitisation_sequence.then: image and transcribe taxon names on folders
digitisation_sequence.next: QR-code and image individual drawing sheets
digitisation_sequence.catalogue: catalogue pages have already been imaged; transcription is a stated next step
digitisation_sequence.interpretive_note: The modern digitisation deliberately begins from drawings because they carry sample numbers and descriptive information needed to build a taxonomic backbone for the other collection components.

research_result: Grunow is now the strongest sample-number case in the project. A single historical number can coordinate unmounted matter, mounted slides, a working catalogue, drawings and annotated books, while the modern museum adds a new stable-identifier layer without discarding the old sample-number logic.

comparison_with_cole_cajal.Cajal: modern catalogue retains successive cabinet, inventory and archival addresses for the same slide
comparison_with_cole_cajal.Grunow: sample number crosses material states and media inside one scientific working collection before later museum digitisation

exact_next_action: Choose one sample number explicitly cited in the 2022/2023 NHM Grunow studies and close it across catalogue entry, surviving raw material/capsule, historical slide if extant, drawing, annotated book reference and current JACQ/QR identifier. Stop after one or two fully closed exemplars rather than inventorying the entire collection.
